source.title: Annihilation of Spurious Minima in Two-Layer ReLU Networks

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analytically studies whether adding neurons changes spurious minima into saddles in two-layer ReLU teacher–student networks. It analyzes Hessian spectra at specified critical-point families, rather than measuring gradient-descent outcomes or frequencies of convergence.
record.gate_note: The paper holds weights fixed and studies critical points and Hessian spectra; it does not run training. Its CIFAR, initialization, depth, learning-rate, and normalization versions are not tested. Empirical detection observations cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes Hessian stability of selected critical-point families, not how often gradient descent from standard initialization reaches spurious minima. These landscape results suggest a mechanism relevant to V2 but do not establish its training-outcome claims. The reported convergence-frequency observations are attributed to prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors show that additional neurons can turn particular symmetric spurious-minimum families into saddles while leaving their loss essentially unchanged. They interpret the resulting descent directions as a mechanism enabling gradient-based escape, without measuring training outcomes. They also establish persistence of the spectral classifications under sufficiently small target perturbations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives a mathematical Hessian analysis of fixed critical-point families in a Gaussian-input, squared-loss, two-layer ReLU teacher–student model. It does not run gradient descent or measure convergence frequencies from initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect depends on the symmetry family and number of added neurons; for the ∆Sd−1 type I family, the effect of adding one neuron differs between d = 10 and d = 100.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected symmetric spurious-minimum families become saddles after one or two additional neurons, with the required increment depending on symmetry and dimension. Other selected families remain minima after one extra neuron.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the specified Gaussian-input, squared-loss two-layer ReLU teacher–student model, mild over-parameterization can change the local stability of particular critical-point families by introducing negative Hessian eigenvalues.

record.problems: The results concern specified symmetric critical-point families and Hessian stability, not measured gradient-descent convergence or the probability of reaching minima. Some supplementary conclusions are qualified as likely or as holding for sufficiently large d. The paper notes that additional spurious-minimum families may appear and may not be annihilated by adding two neurons.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying study results were left out. Cited empirical observations about SGD detection from [19] were excluded because they are prior-work results, not results of this study.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on size, stopping and regularization.

Gradient-descent convergence frequencies from standard initialization; their increase as teacher and student grow together; and their reduction with one or two additional student neurons over widths 6–20.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Learning-rate thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics and convergence or divergence during training.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The rows describe legitimate landscape results, but their observed/absent states cannot be transferred to V2's claims about training outcomes. Surviving local minima can coexist with sharply reduced probabilities of reaching them.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, gradient training from random initialization, model size and training duration.

The paper does not measure how often gradient descent from standard initialization ends in spurious minima, nor sweep teacher and student widths together over 6 to 20 neurons. It studies Hessian stability for specified symmetric families as neurons are added.
Depth, shortcuts, batch normalization, and training error in plain or residual convolutional networks.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss dynamics, and curvature during gradient training.
Batch normalization effects on training speed, accuracy, or learning-rate tolerance; normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I critical-point family with isotropy ∆Sd
rows.operation_detail: Hessian spectral analysis of the type I family
rows.value: The family is a family of minima.
rows.note: The paper analyzes this symmetric critical-point family, not gradient-descent convergence.
rows.check: Local-minimum status does not measure gradient-descent convergence frequency.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I critical-point family with isotropy ∆Sd
rows.operation_detail: Analyze the family after adding one neuron; compute Hessian spectrum
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue signs and descent directions
rows.value: Non-degenerate saddles; negative eigenvalue associated to the standard representation; exactly d − 1 descent directions.
rows.note: The paper reports a local stability change, not an optimization-run success rate.
rows.check: Creating d − 1 descent directions does not establish how often training avoids spurious minima.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I and type II critical-point families with isotropy ∆(Sd−1 × S1)
rows.operation_detail: Hessian spectral analysis of the type I and type II families
rows.note: These are analytically characterized families of critical points.
rows.check: Existence of selected spurious-minimum families does not measure convergence frequency. The family statements require the dimensional conditions underlying the asymptotic analysis.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I and type II critical-point families with isotropy ∆(Sd−1 × S1)
rows.operation_detail: Analyze the families after adding one neuron; compute Hessian spectrum
rows.value: The families remain spurious minima; trivial and standard-representation eigenvalues are strictly positive.
rows.uncertainty: Eigenvalues in Table 1 are given to four decimal places, modulo O(d−1/2)-terms.
rows.note: The added neuron does not annihilate these families in the stated setting.
rows.check: Persistence of selected minima does not show that the reduction in convergence frequency claimed by V2 is absent. Qualify the value as applying for sufficiently large d: the type I point is a saddle at d = 10.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I and type II critical-point families with isotropy ∆(Sd−1 × S1)
rows.operation_detail: Analyze the families after adding two neurons; use Hessian spectrum and interlacing
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue signs and descent directions
rows.value: Non-degenerate saddles with at least a (d − 2)-dimensional space of descent directions.
rows.uncertainty: The 2 × 2 submatrix eigenvalues are given modulo O(d−1/2)-terms: 0.8060… and −0.1198….
rows.note: The paper proves this transition for the stated families; it also notes that other families may appear and may not be annihilated by adding two neurons.
rows.check: The saddle transition does not measure training success. The displayed submatrix eigenvalues 0.8060 and −0.1198 concern the type II calculation; they should not be presented as numerical results for both types.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I critical-point family with isotropy ∆Sd−1
rows.operation_detail: Compare Hessian spectrum after adding one neuron
rows.baseline: k = d, d = 10: spurious minimum, as stated in Section A.4
rows.value: The type I critical point becomes a saddle.
rows.uncertainty: Table 2 gives eigenvalues to four decimal places.
rows.note: The text explicitly contrasts this result with d = 100 at the same neuron increment.
rows.check: The saddle classification is supported by the negative standard-representation eigenvalue −0.00230, but it does not measure convergence frequency.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I critical-point family with isotropy ∆Sd−1
rows.operation_detail: Compare Hessian spectrum after adding one neuron
rows.value: The type I critical point is a spurious minimum.
rows.uncertainty: Table 2 gives eigenvalues to four decimal places.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says the one-neuron addition yields a saddle at d = 10 but a spurious minimum at d = 100.
rows.check: A surviving spurious minimum at d = 100 does not establish absence of improved training success. This dimension also exceeds V2's stated tested widths.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network; type I critical-point family with isotropy ∆Sd−1
rows.operation_detail: Analyze the family after adding two neurons; compute Hessian spectrum
rows.value: The type I critical point becomes a saddle.
rows.uncertainty: Table 2 gives eigenvalues to four decimal places.
rows.note: The authors say it is most likely a saddle for all d ≥ 4, and certainly for sufficiently large d.
rows.check: The saddle classification is supported by the negative eigenvalue −0.03432, but it does not measure convergence frequency. This dimension exceeds V2's stated tested widths.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: At d = 100 one extra neuron leaves a spurious minimum, while adding two neurons makes it a saddle (R7–R8).
